say: You Didn't Know Your Money Loses Purchasing Power While Sitting Still.
What if I told you that doing absolutely nothing with your money could make it worth less?
Sounds impossible, right?
Imagine you hide one thousand dollars in a drawer and completely forget about it.
Ten years later, you open that drawer.
Good news! Your one thousand dollars is still there.
But here's the problem.
The things you could buy with that money might now cost much more.
Imagine a shopping cart full of groceries costs one hundred dollars today.
If prices rise by an average of three percent every year, that same cart could cost around one hundred thirty-four dollars in ten years.
Your money hasn't changed.
But its buying power has.
And here's what makes this interesting.
You don't actually need to spend money to lose some of its value.
Inflation can do that while your cash is sitting completely still.
Now, money in a savings account might earn interest that helps offset inflation.
But cash hidden under your mattress?
It earns absolutely nothing.
So here's the lesson.
The number printed on your money can stay the same forever…
But what that money can buy won't necessarily stay the same.
You didn't know that about money.
